name: navarro-1985
label: Navarro, Santamaría & Bescós 1985 accommodation-dependent schematic eye (regression fixture)
citation: Navarro R, Santamaría J, Bescós J. Accommodation-dependent model of the human eye with aspherics. J Opt Soc Am A 2(8):1273-1281, 1985. Table 1 (relaxed surfaces, indices) and Table 4 (accommodation dependence).
verificationNote: Set verified:true once the paraxial power test (Task 1.6) reproduces the published 60.42 D within 0.05 D and the image of infinity lands on the retina.
wavelengthNote: Table 1 indices are quoted for the sodium d line; the model's dispersion (Table 2) is not transcribed here. Stored under index555 per the schema; the 555 vs 589 nm difference (~0.1 D) is accepted for the regression fixture.
referenceAgeNote: The 1985 model has no age dependence; 30 is a nominal adult age used for amplitude lookups.
role: regression fixture only; not offered as a UI preset at release (spec §4.1)

accommodation.description: Lens and anterior chamber as functions of accommodation A (diopters), Table 4. L = ln(1 + A). anteriorRadius = R_a0 + anteriorRadiusPerLn * L; posteriorRadius = R_p0 + posteriorRadiusPerLn * L; thickness = t0 + thicknessPerLn * L; anteriorChamberDepth = ACD0 + chamberDepthPerLn * L; index = n0 + indexCoeff * (10 A + A^2); anteriorConic = Q_a0 + anteriorConicPerLn * L; posteriorConic = Q_p0 + posteriorConicPerLn * L. The vitreous thickness is held at its relaxed value, so the axial length grows by 0.05 L.
accommodation.unverifiedNote: Radius, thickness, chamber depth, and index coefficients were confirmed against excerpts of Table 4 on 2026-10-26. The two conic coefficients could not be confirmed from the reachable excerpts and are retained from the secondary literature; confirm against the paper before relying on them.
